paper_title: How Much Does the Hint Matter? Scope Conditions for Hindsight Self-Distillation in Financial Reasoning

sections.title: Abstract
sections.content: Financial institutions operating under data-residency constraints are restricted to open-weight models small enough to locally host, which trail frontier systems on multi-step quantitative reasoning. On-policy distillation narrows such gaps by supervising a student on its own rollouts, but traditional OPD requires a strong external teacher, and on-policy self-distillation (OPSD) conditions on a full reference solution. We ask how much of that signal is necessary. We present Fin-SD, a localized hindsight self-distillation recipe for multi-step reasoning. Given a problem the student fails, the student itself identifies the first incorrect reasoning step and writes a short critique of that step. We truncate the student's trajectory immediately before the error (aiming to obtain a correct prefix), condition a frozen copy of the student on the same prefix plus the hint, and distill that hint-conditioned teacher into the student over a short rollout under reverse KL. No external model contributes a gradient. We apply Fin-SD to GPT-OSS-20B on a custom multi-step financial reasoning benchmark that requires deriving formula inputs from realistic scenarios via accounting conventions. We find: (i) replacing the critique with a generic-feedback control matches Fin-SD's entire 3.03 pp accuracy gain over the base model on the FinanceReasoning Hard subset, suggesting the gain comes from where supervision is applied, not hint content; (ii) the model writing the hint does not need to be stronger than the model receiving it: hints from same-family GPT-OSS-120B, at roughly 6x the parameters, yield no materially greater benefits than self-written hints; and (iii) Fin-SD matches on-policy self-distillation from full reference solutions on accuracy while generating 9.5% fewer tokens. With Fin-SD, general reasoning on MMLU-Pro and a fourteen-metric compliance audit on FinTrust show no material regression.

sections.title:
1 Introduction
Deploying Large Language Models (LLMs) in the financial sector
requires careful balancing of performance and regulatory compli-
ance.
sections.content: The first compliance requirement is data residency. Customer records, positions, and internal analyses frequently cannot leave institutional infrastructure, which rules out API access to frontier models and confines deployment to open-weight models served on-premise. Latency and hardware budgets only tighten this further. The second is behavioral assurance. model used in an advisory or analytical capacity is subject to institutional obligations around disclosure, fiduciary care, and the handling of client information. Post-training cannot be allowed to silently erode the behaviors that make model acceptable to deploy; however, domain fine-tuning is known to degrade instruction-following and other post-trained behaviors acquired during alignment [2, 9]. Data residency pushes practitioners toward small, open-weight models. However, these models underperform on exactly the multistep quantitative reasoning that financial analysis demands, unless they are given the fine-tuning that can compromise behavioral assurance. We examine methods for rectifying this. One of the easiest ways to close capability gaps is distillation, and recent work has converged on on-policy distillation (OPD): sample trajectories from the student, then have teacher score each token of those trajectories, typically via per-token reverse KL divergence [1, 4, 9]. Grounding supervision in student-generated states avoids the exposure bias that afflicts training on teacher trajectories, ICAIF26, November, 2026, Milan, Italy Yu and Gorlla and supplies much denser signal than outcome-based reinforcement learning. On-policy self-distillation (OPSD) [15] removes the external teacher by using the student itself, granted privileged information, as its own teacher. HINT-SD [14] sharpens this further for long-horizon agents, applying feedback-conditioned distillation only at the failure-relevant turns rather than uniformly across the failed trajectory. This paper asks how much privileged information self-distillation teacher actually needs, and whether the resulting method is practical post-training recipe under the constraints above (increasing performance while maintaining compliance and cost-effectiveness). Our contributions are as follows: (1) We show that replacing the full hint with fixed genericfeedback control does not materially degrade any of the three metrics, and matches the gain over base (+3.36 pp accuracy, vs Fin-SDs +3.03). This leads us to hypothesize that problemspecific guidance is unnecessary once the mistake is properly localized. (2) Consistent with this, the model writing the hint does not need to be stronger than the model receiving it. On corpus where non-arithmetic failures are dominated by convention selection, 20B model is able to localize the error with the ground-truth answer in hand well enough that swapping out the hint writer for stronger model with roughly 6 the parameters does not make significant difference in accuracy. (3) We present Fin-SD, hindsight self-distillation recipe for multistep finance reasoning. Fin-SD localizes the first faulty clause of failed reasoning trajectory using the students own weights, truncates there, and distills hint-conditioned frozen copy of the student into the student under reverse KL over 100-token rollout. (4) We show that hint matches full solution on accuracy, at lower cost. Comparing Fin-SD against OPSD, we find that it matches OPSDs accuracy (72.19% for Fin-SD vs OPSDs 70.42%), and Fin-SD generates 9.5% fewer tokens at evaluation and is directionally more reliable on in-budget completion rate (+2.44 pp). (5) We demonstrate that the distillation process does not observably hurt compliance and general reasoning, reporting MMLUPro [13] and FinTrust [6] performance for model trained with Fin-SD. (6) We construct corpus of difficult, multi-step financial reasoning problems from the FinanceReasoning function library [12]. Rather than relying on explicit parameters, each problem presents realistic market, timeline, or corporate accounting scenario requiring the user to apply strict financial definitions and conventions to derive key inputs. These derived inputs feed into core financial function to yield an intermediate metric, which is then mapped to single, unambiguous, and easily verifiable final numerical answer. This distinguishes it from benchmarks that assess information extraction or simple formula application as well as rubric-based benchmarks.

sections.title:
2 Related Work
2.1 From offline to on-policy distillation
Classical knowledge distillation trains a student to match a teacher’s
output distribution on a fixed dataset [5], with sequence-level vari-
ants training on teacher-generated outputs [8]. Both are off-policy:
the contexts seen in training are the teacher’s, not the student’s.
On long generations this produces compounding error, since the
student is never trained on recovery from its own mistakes.
sections.content: On-policy distillation addresses this by sampling rollouts from the student and evaluating the teacher on student-visited prefixes. GKD [1] introduced the formulation for autoregressive LMs and analyzed the choice of divergence; MiniLLM [4] argued for reverse KL on the grounds that its mode-seeking behavior prevents the student from spreading mass over regions the teacher considers unlikely; Lu and Thinking Machines Lab [9] give practical recipe using per-token reverse KL as policy-gradient advantage, and note that because no completed rollout is needed to compute the signal, partial rollouts sufficea property we exploit.

sections.title:
2.2 Self-distillation and privileged context
Context distillation [11] trains a model using a context-augmented
version of itself as a teacher, internalizing privileged information
so it can be reproduced without context at inference. Because the
teacher and student share weights, this avoids inheriting an external
model’s artifacts (e.g., verbosity or refusal behaviors).
sections.content: Zhao et al. [15] instantiate this idea directly for reasoning as onpolicy self-distillation (OPSD). The teacher policy conditions on privileged information (a verified reference solution) while the student policy sees only the question, and training minimizes the per-token divergence between the two distributions along the students own rollouts. They report superior token efficiency relative to reinforcement learning (RL) methods on mathematical reasoning benchmarks. HINT-SD [14] combines this with targeted supervision for longhorizon agents. Its observation is that in failed trajectory most turns are already successful or neutral, so distilling uniformly across the trajectory spends the signal on positions that need no correction; it therefore uses hindsight over the complete trajectory to select failure-relevant action spans and applies feedback-conditioned distillation only there. It reports gains over RL and full-trajectory distillation on multi-step tool use benchmarks. Our work adapts this to different domain. Where HINT-SD operates over multi-turn action spans in agentic environments, we operate over reasoning steps within single chain of thought, localizing to the first clause at which the derivation goes wrong.

sections.title:
2.3 Financial reasoning benchmarks
Financial reasoning benchmarks have historically emphasized sen-
timent and classification or extractive question answering over
filings [7]. FinQA [3] and TAT-QA [16] introduced numerical rea-
soning over hybrid table-and-text contexts, but individual questions
typically require few arithmetic operations and present necessary
quantities explicitly.
sections.content: How Much Does the Hint Matter? Scope Conditions for Hindsight Self-Distillation in Financial Reasoning ICAIF26, November, 2026, Milan, Italy Figure 1: Overview of Fin-SD. The student is sampled on training problem and judged against the ground truth. On failures, frozen copy of the student receives the query, the failing trajectory, and the answer, and returns the first faulty step 𝑘, short critique ℎ, and an error type; pure arithmetic slips are dropped without gradient. The trajectory is truncated immediately before k, so both policies condition on the on-policy prefix before the localized error, with the frozen teacher also receiving ℎ. The student minimizes the per-token KL between the two next-token distributions over an = 100 rollout. At each epoch boundary, the failure set is re-mined and the teacher re-frozen. Crucially, existing benchmarks bypass the critical step of using financial logic to construct function inputs rather than merely extracting explicitly stated variables. Our training corpus is structured explicitly around this challenge. FinanceReasoning [12] is the closest existing fit: its Hard subset comprises 238 problems requiring the composition of multiple financial formulas, with Python-formatted solutions and precise answers, and it releases library of 3,133 financial functions. We use boththe function library to seed corpus construction, and the Hard subset for evaluation. For behavioral evaluation we use FinTrust [6], which assesses seven compliance dimensions in financial contexts.

Three policies are involved, all of which are the student in Fin-SD:
sections.content: Student (𝜋𝜃 ): the model being optimized. In all experiments this is GPT-OSS-20B [10]. Teacher (𝜋𝜙 ): frozen copy of the students own weights, prompted with an additional hint. The teacher is contextaugmented instantiation of the student, not separate model. We re-freeze it at each epoch boundary: during epoch 𝑒, 𝜙 = 𝜃 (𝑒 1) , the students weights at the end of the previous epoch. The distillation target therefore improves as the student does, rather than remaining pinned to the initialization. Hint model (𝜋𝐻 ): frozen model used only for error localization and critique generation. It is not distilled from, and therefore does not contribute gradient. In Fin-SD it is the frozen teachers own weights (self); we ablate against GPT-OSS-120B (120b) in Section 6.1. Because 𝜋𝜙 and 𝜋𝜃 share weights and differ only in the context they receive, the method is form of context distillation [11]: the aim is to internalize the behavior the hint induces, so that it is reproduced without the hint at inference.

Given a problem (𝑥, 𝑦∗) on which the student fails (Section 4.1), let

The critique names, for example, the convention the solver should have recognized or the correct way to apply critical concept, and takes the form Your logic diverges when 𝑋 . . . Assume 𝑌 . The informational content of ℎ turns out to be largely dispensable; we isolate it in Section 5.3. Failures whose only error is arithmetic carry no useful signal about reasoning, and in practice would be avoided at the harness level with calculator tool. We therefore have 𝜋𝐻 additionally classify each failure as reasoning error or an arithmetic/rounding slip, and suppress the weight update for the latter. Such items still count as incorrect in all reported accuracies; only the gradient is withheld. An informal audit of the classifier shows that it achieves 96% accuracy (48 out of 50 items correct).

sections.title:
4 Experimental Setup
4.1 Financial reasoning corpus
Function curation. We seed from the library of 3,133 Python-
formatted financial functions released with FinanceReasoning [12].
To remove trivial operations, each function is graded on an 8-point
difficulty scale by an LLM grader (GPT-OSS-120B); we retain func-
tions scoring ≥ 3. Retained functions pass to a viability judge
(DeepSeek-V4-Flash) verifying that each can support a word prob-
lem with a single correct answer, yielding 295 formulas.
sections.content: 1Because models struggle to return exact token positions, we have the model return quote with the erroneous clause repeated verbatim, which is then indexed to character position for truncation. Problem generation. For each formula, we synthesize context-rich, multi-step financial reasoning problems using GPT-5.5. The design How Much Does the Hint Matter? Scope Conditions for Hindsight Self-Distillation in Financial Reasoning ICAIF26, November, 2026, Milan, Italy Corpus item and training example Query 𝑥. An investor is acquiring 12-unit apartment building on January 1 for $2,400,000. Each unit is expected to rent for $1,850 per month. The property is also expected to generate $750 per month from parking and laundry. The investor underwrites annual vacancy loss at 5% of gross scheduled rent. Annual operating expenses are projected as follows: property taxes $31,200, insurance $8,400, commonarea utilities $14,400, and repairs/management/maintenance $35,000. The acquisition is financed with loan equal to 75% of the purchase price. The annual mortgage payments will total $122,400. At closing, the investor must pay the down payment, acquisition closing costs equal to 2% of the purchase price, an immediate roof repair costing $70,000, and lender-required cash reserve of $18,000. The investors minimum acceptable first-year pre-tax cash yield on actual cash invested is 7.50%. By how many percentage points does the propertys first-year pre-tax cash yield on actual cash invested exceed or fall short of the investors 7.50% hurdle rate? Round to the nearest 0.01 percentage points, and state whether it exceeds or falls short. Solution: Phase 1 input derivation. Annualize monthly rents at 12 units 12 months, apply the 5% vacancy haircut to gross scheduled rent only (not ancillary income), and read actual cash invested as down payment + closing costs + immediate capex + lender reserve annual pre-tax cash flow = $50,680, total cash invested = $736,000. Phase 2 core function. Calculate cash on cash return with annual pre-tax cash flow $50,680 and total cash invested $736,000 6.8859% first-year pre-tax cash yield. Phase 3 verifiable closing. Compare against the investors stated 7.50% hurdle: 6.8859% 7.50% 𝑦 = 0.61 percentage points (falls short). . . . truncate [remaining steps, disTraining: Student trajectory. [step 1, correct] . . . [step 𝑘 1, correct] [step 𝑘: So vacancy loss = 0.05 * 275,400 = 13,770.] carded] Hint preamble. The reasoning above is fully correct. The following hint refers to an error originally made at this current step that is not yet visible in the trace above. Do not apologize, acknowledge this hint, or explain the error. Silently apply the correction and continue directly with the next step of the calculation. [Hint] Hint (self). Your logic diverges when you define the base for vacancy loss. Assume vacancy loss is calculated only on the scheduled rent from the apartment units, because the term gross scheduled rent typically refers to the rental income from the units and excludes other income like parking and laundry. Hint (placebo variant - Section 5.3). Your mistake is conceptual. Figure 2: One item from the training corpus, carried through the three generation phases of Section 4.1 and then through the localization and truncation of Section 3.2. target is problem where key inputs are intentionally not specified directly, but must instead be derived from standard finance conventions, market scenarios, or financial statements. Each synthesized problem is structured into three distinct phases: (1) Input Derivation: The user must analyze realistic financial scenarios, timelines, or balance sheet data to calculate the exact inputs required for the target formula based on standard industry definitions. (2) Core Function Execution: The derived inputs are evaluated through the target financial function to obtain an intermediate financial metric. (3) Verifiable Closing Mechanism: The intermediate metric is applied to domain-native endpoint, such as comparing internal rate of return against firms threshold or determining precise dollar-value valuation impact. We then perform critique pass using Claude Fable 5, removing contradictory premises and quantities that are truly underdetermined. This focuses the corpus on tasks and ambiguity that competent analyst could confidently resolve. All items were manually reviewed for logical validity and for the existence of unique correct answer under correct convention application. Figure 2 shows single item carried through all three phases, together with the supervision Fin-SD applies to it. The final set contains 220 problems, split 80/20 for training and validation. While we utilize external LLMs to generate synthetic data for training, in practice, the training corpus would be made up of on-premise data, and so this phase does not strictly require an external model. Failure mining. Training instances are the subset on which the student fails. For each (𝑥, 𝑦) we sample 𝜏stud 𝜋𝜃 ( 𝑥) and compare the extracted answer to 𝑦 using an LLM equivalence judge (DeepSeek-V4-Flash) tolerant of formatting and rounding differences (in deployment, well-designed deterministic parser would suffice as well). Correct instances are discarded; the remainder form Dfail, the input to Algorithm 1. We further filter this by excluding problems that the student is unable to output an answer to within the token budget, as they may be too difficult for the student at first. This reduces the potential training set to around 60 questions per epoch, with the student gradually moving to harder questions over time. Of these 60, around 35 are arithmetic errors, so the final training set is roughly 25 problems per epoch.

sections.title:
4.3 Evaluation and statistics
We evaluate on the FinanceReasoning Hard subset [12], which is
comprised of 238 multi-step finance problems. We report accuracy
(fraction solved), in-budget completion rate (fraction of attempts
that adhere to the 8192-token budget, hereafter simply completion
rate), and total tokens (cumulative generation over the full evalua-
tion).
sections.content: We compare Fin-SD against three baselinesOPSD, SFT on reference solutions, and the base GPT-OSS-20B, and we ablate hint content, hint writer, KL direction, and rollout length. Fin-SD is trained under five seeds (7, 42, 72, 2, 27), as is each ablation cell and OPSD; SFT is trained under three seeds (7, 42, 72), and the base model is evaluated under five independent runs. All runs are served at BF16 precision and share the identical 238-problem set. We report means over seeds with sample standard deviations and 𝑡-based 95% confidence intervals. Sources of run-to-run variation. Decoding temperature is 0.0, so the spread across runs is not sampling variance. Sources of variation include training seeds, inference non-determinism, and LLM-asjudge. The latter two are measurement noise rather than model training variance. sections.title: 5.2 Hints match full reference solutions at
sections.content: lower cost Fin-SD reaches 72.19% against OPSDs 70.42%, reduces token spend by 53.6k tokens, or 9.5% (508.5k vs 562.1k), and gains 2.44 pp over OPSD (92.19% vs 89.75%). It greatly improves over SFT, which is ineffective here. The interpretation is that hint carries enough of the reference solutions signal to match it on task accuracy, while inducing shorter solution style.

sections.title:
5.3 A vague hint matches a targeted critique
Fin-SD uses informative hints: the critique is of the form “Your
logic diverges when 𝑋 . . . Assume 𝑌 .” To test how much of Fin-SD’s
benefit comes from that content rather than from the machinery
around it, we replace ℎ with a fixed generic-feedback string—“Your
mistake is conceptual”, so that the placebo carries no problem-
specific information. Everything else is held constant.

The SFT interval extends to 16.10 and is clipped at the axis limit (arrow). The placebo does not underperform the full hint on any metric. Accuracy is 72.52%, above Fin-SD by 0.33 pp (Figure 3); completion rate is higher by 0.17 pp and token count lower by 4.7k. All three gaps sit well inside the seed spread. Relative to base, the placebo runs show no significant degradation: +3.36 pp accuracy, +1.18 pp completion rate, and 22.0k fewer tokens. This is consistent with the gains reported above being driven predominantly by where the supervision is applied rather than by what the critique says, assuming sufficiently knowledgeable student/base model. Truncating at 𝑘 returns the student to the on-policy prefix before the localized error and concentrates the whole distillation budget at the position where the derivation actually goes wrong.

sections.title:
5.4 General capability and compliance
An important post-training constraint in highly regulated fields is
that it cannot degrade compliance or general reasoning. We report
two out-of-domain evaluations of Fin-SD.
sections.content: MMLU-Pro. For general reasoning, we evaluate on the MMLU-Pro benchmark, large evaluation suite comprised of just over 12,000 questions spanning variety of fields. To ensure appropriate out-ofdomain evaluation, we exclude the business and economics fields, reducing the benchmark to just over 10,000 questions. We find that general reasoning performance is near-identical, as is execution rate and mean tokens. The slight drop in overall accuracy is primarily driven by 5.47 pp drop in chemistry, with all other categories moving less than 2% in either direction. We theorize that this is due to the significant number of semantic collisions between finance and chemistry, e.g. yield, concentration, etc. How Much Does the Hint Matter? Completion rate moves by only 0.50 and 0.34 pp respectively, and token count rises 12.4k and 20.0k. No pairwise contrast between hint writers in Figure 3 approaches significance on accuracy. This is consistent with the earlier hint information result; it appears that the bottleneck for improvement is the ability of the student to self-correct, not the quality of the information provided in the hint. It also suggests the benefit is robust to coarse localization rather than sensitive to step-level boundary precision (which stronger model would presumably be better at). HINT-SD [14] reports the opposite: substituting stronger external feedback writer for its self-generated feedback improves results substantially on both of its benchmarks. There are two possible explanations for this discrepancy: (1) HINT-SDs student is 4B model, which may not reliably localize its own error even with the ground-truth answer in hand, whereas at 20B that diagnostic step is closer to saturated. (2) HINT-SDs feedback is largely API documentationa missing credential, an undefined variable, renamed endpointand supplies information the student does not have, whereas our critiques name financial conventions that Western-pretrained 20B model plausibly holds in weights and fails to select. The larger model size that we study also supports this latent knowledge argument. Either way, industry-scale open Western models (such as GPTOSS-120B) are large enough that we view our result as likely more applicable in practice. Furthermore, data residency forbids the use of frontier teacher, so HINT-SDs recommendation to use one is not actionable.

sections.title:
6.2 Reverse direction outperforms forward
Fin-SD’s choice of reverse KL over forward KL improves accuracy
by 1.26 pp (70.93% to 72.19%), completion rate by 0.76 pp, and uses
20.6k fewer tokens. The same choice under the 120b writer improves
accuracy by 0.93 pp, completion rate by 0.92 pp, and uses 13.0k
less tokens. The gain is therefore in the same direction on all three
metrics under both writers.
sections.content: ICAIF26, November, 2026, Milan, Italy Yu and Gorlla The consistency of sign across metrics and writers suggests real but modest effect, and this finding is consistent with the modeseeking argument for reverse KL in the distillation literature [4, 9, 14].

sections.title:
7 Limitations
Self-distillation ceiling. The teacher is a copy of the student, so
gains are bounded by what hint-conditioning can elicit from the
student’s pre-training exposure. Re-freezing the teacher at each
epoch boundary raises this ceiling, but does not remove it. Simi-
larly, the writer-invariance likely holds only up to some difficulty
threshold, after which the student is unable to diagnose its own
mistakes.
sections.content: Trainingevaluation overlap. 17 of the 295 formulas seeding the corpus appear in the solutions of 22 of the 238 evaluation items, so this is in-domain transfer, though problem-writing philosophy differs greatly between training corpus and benchmark. Lack of tuning. We did not extensively tune hyperparameters or refine prompts. Our training schedule utilized an extended linear warmup phase that occupied 15 out of 20 total optimization steps, which converged well but likely limited training gains. Limited training corpus. 220 problems is modest, and failure mining means we only train on subset each epoch. Furthermore, we do not include tasks which have multiple justifiable assumptions, as these would require rubric-based grading.

sections.title:
8 Conclusion
We adapted targeted hindsight self-distillation from long-horizon
agents to multi-step financial reasoning, and investigated how much
privileged information a self-distillation teacher actually needs. We
find that a short critique locating the first faulty reasoning step
matches full-solution on-policy self-distillation on accuracy while
producing a shorter, more reliably executable solution style at 9.5%
lower token cost.
sections.content: This is further reinforced by our hint content comparison, where we find that generic hint that provides no problem-specific information performs just as well as one that provides the correct next step, which is consistent with the main benefit being the choice of supervision sitea repaired, on-policy prefix at the first faulty steprather than the content of the feedback. Consistent with this, the model writing the hint does not need to be stronger than the model receiving it. On corpus where nonarithmetic failures are dominated by convention selection, 20B model is able to localize the error with the ground-truth answer in hand well enough that using same-family hint writer with roughly 6 the parameters makes no measurable difference. Therefore, Fin-SD provides post-training recipe with no external model contributing gradientan important result for an institution that cannot send its data to frontier API. Future work could include testing Fin-SD on student models of varying sizes, or in different domains, such as law.
